inputs: head files read beyond the context: Verifiers/CSharpCodeFixVerifier`2+Test.cs and the VerifyCS aliases of all SourceGenerator test classes
summary: Test-only change: the source generator test verifier now defaults to C# 7.3 (applied through CreateParseOptions, so test input and generated code are compiled at 7.3), and the tests whose input needs newer syntax opt in explicitly. tests.detects_original_regression shows the new default catches the #1925 regression (61 listed tests fail with CS8370 in the generated resolver on the pre-#1926 generator, all passing with the old test files), and the full suite passes 123/123. I additionally read the analyzer verifier and the VerifyCS aliases: the changed CSharpSourceGeneratorCodeFixVerifier default has no users. All clauses met; two info notes.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: Both the Test.LanguageVersion property and the RunDefaultAsync parameter default to CSharp7_3, the value is applied to the parse options, and the regression check shows generated code failing with CS8370 at 7.3 on the pre-fix generator.

evidence.quote: compile the test input and the generated code at C# 7.3
public LanguageVersion LanguageVersion { get; set; } = LanguageVersion.CSharp7_3;

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: Every explicit opt-in I read has input needing more than C# 7.3 (records -> 9, record struct -> 10, #nullable/notnull -> 8/9) while the class/struct rows were lowered to 7.3, and the full suite passing at the 7.3 default shows no test that needs newer syntax was left on the default.

evidence.quote: must set that language version explicitly, and only those

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: facts.json classifies all 6 changed files as test, public_api shows no src change, and tests.full_suite passes 123/123 with 123/123 on base.

evidence.quote: The change touches only test code

findings.title: Two generic-constraint tests pin C# 9 although their input uses C# 8 features
findings.claim: Generics_Constraints_NullableReferenceType and Generics_Constraints_ReferenceType_Nullable use #nullable enable / nullable constraints (C# 8) but are pinned to C# 9, so C# 9-only syntax emitted by the generator for these constraint shapes would not be caught. I did not run them at C# 8, so whether 8 suffices is unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Try LanguageVersion.CSharp8 for these two tests and keep the lowest version that compiles the input.

findings.title: CSharpSourceGeneratorCodeFixVerifier default changed but the verifier is unused
findings.claim: No test class aliases CSharpSourceGeneratorCodeFixVerifier (I checked every VerifyCS alias at head), so this one-line change has no effect today; harmless and consistent, but it is not exercised by the suite.

evidence.quote: public LanguageVersion LanguageVersion { get; set; } = LanguageVersion.CSharp7_3;
